newsitem.title: BRAZIL: IMF economists keep quiet upon return to Brazil.
newsitem.headline: IMF economists keep quiet upon return to Brazil.

text.p: Economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), who last year upset Brazilian officials with warnings over rising debt, maintained a more discreet tone when they returned to Brasilia Monday.

Vito Tanzi, the IMF's director of fiscal affairs, steered clear of references to Brazil in a speech to a seminar on public finances and afterwards declined comment on the country's economic situation.
"Of course, we from the fund always like faster progress, but I'm not in a position to talk," he said.

At a similar seminar last September, Tanzi created a stir by saying Brazil's debt levels, then 33.9 percent of gross domestic product, were "worrisome" and suggested high interest rates and slow economic growth would add to the burden.
"We don't need any Dr Tanzis coming to warn us," Central Bank international affairs director Gustavo Franco retorted in response to the comments.

This time, the IMF team appeared less than willing to talk about Brazil. Another official specialized in Brazilian affairs said she was unable to comment pending conclusion of a study into the country's fiscal and economic position.
Instead, it was Finance Ministry executive secretary Pedro Parente who answered questions from reporters about whether Brazil had improved since the last visit of the IMF.
"Last year, the operational deficit was around the five percent mark and now it's about 3.5 percent," Parente said. "The debt-GDP ratio has stabilized at 34.4 percent."
